specAnchors.text: understand how an increase in greenhouse gases results in an enhanced greenhouse effect and that this may lead to global warming and its consequences

primer.text: The greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life, but human emissions are turning it up. This note explains the natural trapping of heat by greenhouse gases, then traces the consequences of the enhanced effect: warming oceans, extreme weather, habitat loss and falling biodiversity.

modules.title: The Natural Greenhouse Machine
modules.opening: The greenhouse effect is the natural process that keeps Earth liveable: radiation from the sun warms the surface, the surface re-emits heat, and greenhouse gases in the atmosphere trap part of that heat before it escapes to space.
keyPoints: The sun emits radiation that enters the atmosphere of the Earth.
The surface absorbs the energy and re-emits it as heat, in the form of infrared radiation.
Some heat escapes to space, while greenhouse gases absorb and trap the rest in the atmosphere.
This natural trapping is what keeps the planet warm enough for life to survive.

low.restatement: Sunlight warms the ground, the ground breathes out heat, and the gases hold some of it in.
low.analogy: A car parked in the sun with the windows up — warmth gets in and cannot fully leave.
low.examPointer: Name infrared radiation as the re-emitted heat and give carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour as trappers.

medium.restatement: The sequence matters: solar radiation passes in, the surface absorbs it and re-emits infrared, part of that heat escapes to space and part is absorbed by greenhouse gases, and this balance of trapping is what lifts the planet above freezing and keeps it habitable.
medium.analogy: A duvet over a sleeper: body heat passes into the duvet, and only some of it leaks out.
medium.examPointer: Stress that the natural effect is essential — the enhancement by human emissions is the problem.

modules.title: Turning Up the Thermostat
sourceHeadings: The consequences of an enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming
modules.opening: Human activities raise greenhouse gas levels, so more heat is trapped than nature intends: the average temperature of the Earth climbs above normal, and the resulting global warming reshapes oceans, weather, habitats and species distributions.
keyPoints: The enhanced greenhouse effect arises when human activities raise greenhouse gas levels.
Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and agriculture all add to the trapped heat.
The average temperature of the Earth rises above normal, causing global warming and climate change.
Consequences include melting ice caps, rising seas, extreme weather, habitat loss, falling biodiversity and spreading pests and disease.

low.restatement: More gas means more trapped heat, and the extra warmth reshapes oceans, weather and wildlife.
low.analogy: Turning a thermostat up in every room of the planet at once, with ice melting in the freezer.
low.examPointer: Group the consequences: oceans, extreme weather, habitats, biodiversity, migration and disease.

medium.restatement: The enhancement is anthropogenic — fossil fuel combustion, deforestation and agriculture push gas levels up — and the trapped extra heat raises the average temperature, melting polar ice, lifting seas, intensifying storms, degrading habitats, cutting biodiversity and driving pests and disease into new regions.
medium.analogy: A city whose heating is left running while its cool rooms (the forests) are stripped out, so every system overheats together.
medium.examPointer: For consequence questions, list at least three distinct effects rather than rewording one.

glossary.definition: The natural process in which greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere of the Earth.
The heat radiation that the surface of the Earth emits after absorbing sunlight.
The rise of the average temperature of the Earth above its normal level.
The range and variety of different species of organisms on Earth or within an ecosystem.
